en: 2 eggs
2 thin basturma slices
Half tsp oil
Black pepper, cumin
Baladi bread to serve
Heat the oil in a small pan
Add the basturma slices until lightly browned
Crack the eggs on top and cook until the white sets
Sprinkle pepper and cumin, serve with the bread
1 cup peeled cooked split fava beans
1 small onion, 1 garlic clove
Fresh coriander and dill
1 tsp olive oil, cumin
Lemon to serve
Boil the beans with the onion and garlic until soft
Blend in a processor with the coriander and dill
Add the cumin and oil, blend until creamy
Serve warm with lemon juice

name.en: Ful Medames with Tomato and Lemon

en: Canned fava beans, drained, 250 g
1 medium tomato, diced, and 1 small onion, chopped
1 crushed garlic clove and ground cumin half a tsp
Lemon juice 2 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt and black pepper
Baladi or whole-wheat bread to serve (optional)
Place the drained fava beans in a small pot with a little water, cook over medium heat 5-7 minutes until heated through and some beans start to break down.
Mash half the beans lightly with a fork for a creamy texture while keeping some whole.
Add the garlic, cumin, salt and black pepper and stir.
Pour into a serving plate, drizzle with lemon juice and olive oil, arrange the tomato and onion on top, and serve with bread if desired.

name.en: White Cheese Plate with Tomato and Cucumber

en: Low-fat white cheese 80 g
Medium tomato, sliced, and cucumber, sliced, 150 g total
5 green olives (optional)
A pinch of dried thyme and 1 tsp olive oil
Baladi or whole-wheat bread, 1 slice (40 g)
Fresh mint for garnish (optional)
Arrange the white cheese in the centre of a serving plate.
Arrange the tomato and cucumber slices around it.
Add the olives if desired, sprinkle the thyme and olive oil over the cheese.
Serve with the bread, and garnish with fresh mint if desired.
2 eggs
2 medium tomatoes, diced
Green bell pepper, diced, and chopped onion
1 crushed garlic clove and ground cumin half a tsp
A pinch of sweet paprika and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt, black pepper and baladi bread to serve (optional)
Heat the oil in a pan, brown the onion and bell pepper for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt and black pepper, cook 8-10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Make two small wells in the sauce and crack the eggs into them.
Cover the pan and cook 5-6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft, serve hot with bread if desired.

name.en: Balila (Warm Chickpeas with Cumin and Lemon)

en: Canned chickpeas, drained, 250 g
1 crushed garlic clove and ground cumin 1 tsp
Lemon juice 2 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt, black pepper and a pinch of cayenne pepper (optional)
Chopped parsley for garnish
Baladi bread to serve (optional)
Place the drained chickpeas in a small pot with a little water, cook over medium heat 6-8 minutes until fully heated through.
Add the garlic and cumin and stir for another minute.
Drain excess water, add the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, black pepper and cayenne pepper if desired.
Pour into a serving bowl, garnish with parsley, and serve warm with bread if desired.

name.en: Baked Fiteer Meshaltet with Honey (Light Layered Flatbread)

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Warm water about 35 ml and a pinch of salt
Vegetable oil 1 tsp for the dough
Melted low-fat butter 1 tsp for layering
Honey 1 tbsp to serve
A pinch of sesame seeds for garnish (optional)
Knead the flour with the warm water, salt and oil gradually until a soft dough forms, let it rest 30 minutes.
Roll it out very thin on a lightly floured surface, brush with the melted butter.
Fold the dough several times to form layers, then coil it into a spiral and gently flatten again into a disc.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes until golden and the layers are crisp, drizzle with honey and sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired, and serve hot.

name.en: Beid Maqli bel Kamoon (Fried Eggs with Cumin and Tomato)

en: 2 eggs
1 small tomato, sliced
Ground cumin half a tsp
Salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil
Baladi bread to serve (optional)
Heat the oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add the tomato slices and cook 2-3 minutes until slightly softened.
Crack the eggs over the tomato, sprinkle with cumin, salt and black pepper.
Cook 4-5 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft, serve hot with bread if desired.

name.en: Aish Baladi with Olive Oil and Zaatar

en: Baladi or whole-wheat bread, 1 loaf (80 g)
Olive oil 2 tbsp
Dried thyme (zaatar) 1 tbsp
Medium tomato, sliced, and cucumber, sliced
5 green olives (optional)
A little salt
Cut the bread into pieces or leave it as a whole loaf as desired.
Pour the olive oil into a small dish, sprinkle the thyme over it to form a thick mixture.
Arrange the tomato, cucumber and olives around the oil and thyme dish.
Dip the bread pieces into the oil and thyme, sprinkle with a little salt, and serve with the vegetables.
Thin baladi or whole-wheat bread, 2 loaves (80 g)
Low-fat cottage cheese 60 g
Diced tomato and drained grated cucumber
1 egg
Chopped spring onion, salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the cottage cheese with the tomato, cucumber, egg, spring onion, salt and black pepper until combined.
Spread the mixture evenly over each piece of bread.
Roll tightly into a cylinder, secure the edge with a light press.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with oil, and bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden and crisp.
150 g chicken breast, cubed
200 g chopped molokhia (fresh or frozen)
2 crushed garlic cloves
Dried coriander, 1 tsp oil
White rice to serve
Boil the chicken in 3 cups of water for 20 minutes
Add the molokhia and simmer 10 minutes
Sauté the garlic and dried coriander in the oil
Stir the tempering into the molokhia and serve with rice
Half cup cooked rice
Half cup cooked brown lentils
Quarter cup cooked small pasta
Half cup cooked chickpeas
Oven-crisped onion, tomato sauce and vinegar
Cook the rice, lentils and pasta each separately
Roast the sliced onion in the oven until crisp
Make a tomato sauce with garlic, vinegar and chilli
Layer it all in one plate and add the sauce and onion

name.en: Light Fattah (Layered Rice and Bread with Garlic Vinegar Sauce)

en: Cooked white rice 150 g
Cooked beef, small cubes, 80 g
Toasted baladi or whole-wheat bread, cut into small pieces, 40 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and white vinegar 1 tbsp
Light vegetable or meat stock 100 ml
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp (optional)
Toast the bread pieces in an oven or dry pan until golden and crisp.
Mix the crushed garlic with the vinegar in a small bowl, let it sit 5 minutes.
Heat the stock, add the garlic and vinegar mixture to it.
Arrange the bread in the bottom of a serving dish, add the rice on top, pour the hot stock over it, arrange the meat on top, add the yogurt if desired, and serve immediately.
Boiled cabbage leaves, 8 large leaves
Egyptian or short-grain rice 100 g
Tomato, small dice, and onion, chopped, 100 g total
Chopped parsley and dill
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 1 tbsp
Light vegetable stock 250 ml and salt and black pepper
Mix the rice with the tomato, onion, parsley, dill, garlic, lemon juice, salt and black pepper.
Spread out a cabbage leaf, place a tablespoon of filling at the base, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Repeat with the remaining leaves, arrange them snugly in a pot, one on top of another.
Pour the stock over them, cover and simmer 40-45 minutes until the rice is fully cooked, and serve warm.
Lean minced beef 120 g
Grated onion and finely chopped green bell pepper
Chopped parsley and 1 crushed garlic clove
Ground cumin and mixed spice half a tsp each
1 large flat baladi bread (80 g)
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Knead the minced beef thoroughly with the grated onion, bell pepper, parsley, garlic, cumin, mixed spice, salt and black pepper.
Cut the baladi bread horizontally to open an inner pocket.
Stuff the bread evenly with the meat mixture and press gently to close.
Brush the bread with oil on the outside, bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until the meat is fully cooked and the bread is golden.
Egyptian or short-grain rice 100 g
Low-fat milk 200 ml
Water 100 ml
Low-fat butter 1 tsp
A little salt
A pinch of ground cinnamon for garnish (optional)
Wash the rice and boil it in water for 5 minutes until it starts to soften, drain.
Place it in a small oven-safe dish, add the milk, butter and salt.
Cover the dish tightly with foil.
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until the rice fully absorbs the milk and becomes creamy, sprinkle with cinnamon if desired and serve warm.

name.en: Light Macarona Bechamel (Baked Pasta with Light Bechamel)

en: Cooked whole-wheat pasta 100 g
Lean minced beef 80 g
Chopped onion and diced tomato
Whole-wheat flour 1 tbsp and low-fat milk 200 ml for the bechamel
Low-fat grated cheese 20 g
Salt, black pepper and a pinch of nutmeg
Brown the onion in a dry pan for 3 minutes, add the minced meat and stir until fully cooked.
Add the tomato, salt and black pepper, cook 5 minutes, remove from heat.

For the bechamel, mix the flour with a little cold milk until dissolved, heat the remaining milk in a small pot and gradually add the flour mixture, stirring constantly, until it thickens, add the nutmeg.

Place half the pasta in a small baking dish, add a layer of the meat, cover with the remaining pasta, pour the bechamel over it, sprinkle with cheese, and bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until the top is golden.
Chopped frozen or fresh molokhia leaves 150 g
Peeled medium shrimp 120 g
3 crushed garlic cloves and ground coriander half a tsp
Light vegetable stock 300 ml
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Cooked white rice 110 g
Bring the stock to a boil in a pot, add the chopped molokhia and cook 10-12 minutes until tender.
In a small pan, brown the garlic in the oil for a minute until fragrant, add the coriander and stir for a few seconds.
Add the garlic mixture to the molokhia and stir.
Add the shrimp to the molokhia and cook 4-5 minutes until fully cooked, adjust the salt and black pepper, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Bamya bel Zeit (Okra in Olive Oil and Tomato, Vegetarian) with Rice

en: Fresh or frozen okra 250 g
2 diced tomatoes or light tomato sauce
Chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Ground coriander half a tsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt and black pepper
Cooked white rice 110 g
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pan for 3 minutes.
Add the okra and stir gently for 3 minutes without breaking it.
Add the tomato, ground coriander, salt and black pepper, cover and simmer 15-18 minutes until the okra is fully cooked.
Drizzle with olive oil at the end and serve with the rice.

name.en: Ruz bi Sha'riya (Egyptian Rice with Vermicelli) with Chicken

en: White rice 100 g
Thin vermicelli, broken, 30 g
Cooked, shredded chicken breast 80 g
1 tsp oil and water 200 ml
A little salt
Crispy fried shallots for garnish (optional)
Heat the oil in a pot, brown the broken vermicelli for 2-3 minutes until slightly golden, being careful not to burn it.
Wash the rice and add it to the vermicelli, stir for a minute.
Add the water and salt, cover and simmer 15-18 minutes until the rice is fully cooked and absorbs the water.
Add the shredded chicken and stir gently, garnish with fried shallots if desired and serve hot.
120 g lean lamb, cubed
250 g fresh or frozen okra
1 onion and 2 tomatoes
1 garlic clove, dried coriander
1 tbsp oil
Brown the meat with the onion in the oil 8 minutes
Add the tomato and garlic, cook 15 minutes
Add the okra and half a cup of water
Simmer 20 minutes without stirring too much
150 g lean minced meat
1 grated onion, chopped parsley
3 tomatoes, puréed
1 garlic clove, bell pepper
1 tsp oil, mixed spice
Knead the meat with onion, parsley and spices
Shape into fingers and sear in a pan 5 minutes
Add the tomato, garlic and pepper, bring to a boil
Simmer 15 minutes until the sauce thickens
Lean minced beef 140 g
Grated onion and chopped parsley
1 crushed garlic clove, ground cumin and mixed spice half a tsp each
Salt and black pepper
Cooked white rice 110 g
Sliced tomato to serve (optional)
Knead the minced beef with the grated onion, parsley, garlic, cumin, mixed spice, salt and black pepper thoroughly until it binds together.
Shape into long fingers around metal or water-soaked wooden skewers.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked and golden on the outside.
Serve with the rice and sliced tomato if desired.
White fish fillet 140 g
2 large onions, thinly sliced
2 crushed garlic cloves and ground cumin 1 tsp
Ground coriander half a tsp and a pinch of cardamom (optional)
White rice 110 g and light fish or vegetable stock 200 ml
Lemon juice, salt and black pepper
Brown the onion in a dry pan over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, stirring, until it turns dark and sweet.
Divide the browned onion in half, mash one half and set aside for garnish.
Cook the rice with half the mashed onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, cardamom and stock until fully cooked.
Season the fish with salt, black pepper and lemon juice, bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes, serve over the rice and garnish with the remaining browned onion.

name.en: Grilled Firakh Mashwiya (Egyptian Spiced Chicken) with Rice

en: Skinless chicken thighs 140 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 2 tbsp
Ground cumin, ground coriander and paprika half a tsp each
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp for the marinade
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Cooked white rice 110 g
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, paprika, yogurt, salt and black pepper to make the marinade.
Rub the chicken thoroughly with the marinade and let it sit at least 30 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked and golden on the outside, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Kebda Eskandarani (Alexandrian Spiced Liver) with Bread

en: Beef liver, sliced, 140 g
Green bell pepper, sliced, and 3 crushed garlic cloves
Ground cumin and ground coriander half a tsp each
Chopped hot chili (optional) and white vinegar 1 tsp
1 tsp oil, salt and black pepper
Baladi bread to serve (40 g)
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat, cook the liver for just 2-3 minutes per side until done without becoming tough, set aside.
In the same pan, brown the garlic and bell pepper for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the cumin, coriander and hot chili if desired and stir for a minute.
Return the liver to the pan, add the vinegar, salt and black pepper, stir a final minute and serve with the bread.

name.en: Baked Samak Mashwi (Egyptian Spiced Fish) with Rice

en: White fish fillet 140 g
3 crushed garlic cloves and chopped fresh coriander
Ground cumin and ground coriander half a tsp each
Lemon juice 2 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt, black pepper and a pinch of cayenne pepper (optional)
Cooked white rice 110 g
Mix the garlic, fresh coriander, cumin, ground coriander, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, black pepper and cayenne pepper if desired to make the marinade paste.
Rub the fish thoroughly with the paste and let it sit 15-20 minutes.
Arrange on a lined tray.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until fully cooked, and serve with the rice.

name.en: Grilled Lamb Chops with Egyptian Spices and Rice

en: Lean lamb chops 140 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 1 tbsp
Ground cumin, ground coriander and paprika half a tsp each
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Chopped parsley for garnish
Cooked white rice 110 g
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, paprika, salt and black pepper to make the marinade.
Rub the lamb chops with the marinade and let sit at least 30 minutes.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 16-18 minutes, turning halfway, until cooked, garnish with parsley and serve with the rice.

name.en: Baked Chicken Livers with Onions and Rice

en: Chicken liver, cut into medium pieces, 140 g
2 onions, thinly sliced
2 crushed garlic cloves and ground cumin half a tsp
White vinegar 1 tsp and 1 tsp oil
Salt and black pepper
Cooked white rice 110 g
Brown the onion in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and liver and stir over medium-high heat for just 5-6 minutes until cooked without becoming tough.
Add the cumin, vinegar, salt and black pepper and stir a final minute.
Drizzle with oil and serve with the rice.
Peeled medium shrimp 160 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 2 tbsp
Sweet paprika and ground cumin half a tsp each
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Wooden skewers soaked in water
Cooked white rice 110 g
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, paprika, cumin, salt and black pepper to make the marinade.
Marinate the shrimp in it and let it sit 15-20 minutes.
Thread onto the wooden skewers.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 8-10 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked, and serve with the rice.
1 cup soaked, de-bittered lupini beans
Juice of 1 lemon
A pinch of salt and cumin
1 crushed garlic clove (optional)
A little cold water
Drain the lupini from the soaking water
Toss with the lemon juice, salt and cumin
Add the garlic if you like and a little cold water
Serve chilled in a small cup
1 small piece baladi bread
2 tbsp dukkah (hazelnut, sesame, ground cumin)
1 tsp olive oil
A pinch of salt
Cherry tomatoes to serve
Dip the bread piece into the oil
Then dip it into the dukkah
Add an extra pinch of salt if you like
Serve with cherry tomatoes
Canned chickpeas, drained and dried well, 200 g
1 tsp olive oil
Ground cumin and paprika half a tsp each
A little salt and a pinch of cayenne pepper (optional)
A little lemon juice after roasting
A pinch of garlic powder (optional)
Dry the chickpeas thoroughly with a paper towel to remove as much moisture as possible.
Mix them with the oil, cumin, paprika, salt, cayenne pepper and garlic powder if desired.
Arrange in a single layer on a lined tray.
Bake at 200°C for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until fully crisp, sprinkle with lemon juice after removing and serve once slightly cooled.
Peeled, split fava beans, soaked overnight, 200 g
1 small onion, 2 garlic cloves and fresh coriander
Fresh dill and ground cumin half a tsp
A pinch of baking powder, salt and black pepper
Sesame seeds for coating (optional)
1 tsp oil for brushing
Drain the soaked fava beans well, grind them with the onion, garlic, coriander and dill in a food processor until a coarse, cohesive mixture forms.
Add the cumin, baking powder, salt and black pepper and mix.
Shape the mixture into small patties, dip in sesame seeds if desired.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with oil, and bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Lean minced beef or chicken 100 g
1 small chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Mixed spice and ground cumin half a tsp each
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheets, 4 pieces (60 g)
1 beaten egg for brushing, salt and black pepper
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pan for 3 minutes.
Add the minced meat and stir until fully cooked, add the mixed spice, cumin, salt and black pepper, let the filling cool slightly and add the pine nuts if desired.
Cut each pastry sheet in half, place a spoonful of filling on each half and fold into a triangle, press the edges to seal.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with the beaten egg, and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until golden and crisp.
1 large eggplant (300 g)
1 crushed garlic clove and tahini 1 tbsp
Lemon juice 2 tbsp and olive oil 1 tsp
Salt and a pinch of ground cumin (optional)
Chopped parsley for garnish
Baladi bread or fresh vegetables to serve (optional)
Prick the eggplant several times with a fork, grill under the broiler or roast in a 220°C oven for 35-40 minutes, turning, until fully cooked and the skin is charred.
Let it cool slightly, peel and remove excess seeds if desired.
Mash the flesh with the garlic, tahini, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and cumin until a creamy mixture forms.
Pour into a serving dish, garnish with parsley, and serve with bread or fresh vegetables.
Fine bulgur, soaked 10 minutes, 80 g
Lean minced beef 120 g (divided into two portions)
Grated onion and finely chopped onion
Mixed spice and ground cumin half a tsp each
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Grind half the meat with the soaked bulgur, grated onion and mixed spice in a food processor until a smooth, cohesive dough forms (the shell layer).
Brown the chopped onion in a dry pan for 3 minutes, add the other half of the meat and stir until cooked, add the cumin, salt, black pepper and pine nuts if desired (the filling layer).
Take a small amount of the bulgur dough, shape into a ball and press with your finger to form a hollow, fill with the meat filling and seal into a torpedo shape tapered at both ends.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with oil, and bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

name.en: Baked Gebna Rolls (Cheese and Herb Pastry Rolls)

en: Low-fat cottage cheese 100 g
Low-fat grated feta cheese 40 g
Chopped fresh dill and chopped spring onion
1 egg
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheets, 4 pieces (60 g)
Egg white for brushing, salt and black pepper
Mix the cottage cheese and feta with the dill, spring onion, egg, salt and black pepper until combined.
Place two tablespoons of filling along the edge of each pastry sheet and roll tightly into a thin cylinder, seal the edge with egg white.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with egg white.
Bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Zucchini, grated and well drained, 200 g
Chopped spring onion and chopped fresh dill
1 egg and whole-wheat flour 30 g
Low-fat cottage cheese 30 g
Salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil for brushing
Squeeze the grated zucchini thoroughly with your hands or a clean towel to remove as much water as possible.
Mix it with the spring onion, dill, egg, flour, cheese, salt and black pepper until combined.
Spoon the mixture into small flat mounds on a lined tray.
Brush with oil and bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

name.en: Baked Batata Harra (Spicy Potato Bites with Garlic and Coriander)

en: Potato, small cubes, 250 g
3 crushed garlic cloves and chopped fresh coriander
Chopped hot chili (optional) and lemon juice 1 tbsp
1 tsp oil, salt and black pepper
A pinch of ground cumin
A pinch of sweet paprika
Arrange the potato cubes on a lined tray, brush with oil and sprinkle with salt, black pepper and cumin.
Bake at 220°C for 25-30 minutes, turning every 10 minutes, until golden and crisp.
In a small bowl, mix the garlic, fresh coriander, lemon juice and hot chili if desired.
Remove the potatoes, toss them with the garlic and coriander mixture immediately while hot, sprinkle with paprika and serve immediately.
2 slices crisped wholegrain bread
200 ml low-fat milk
1 tsp honey
A little almonds and raisins
A pinch of cinnamon and vanilla
Toast the bread slices in the oven until crisp
Crumble them into a small baking dish
Warm the milk with the honey and vanilla, pour over
Scatter almonds, raisins and cinnamon, bake 10 minutes
Half cup wholewheat flour
1 egg
Half tsp baking powder
2 tbsp date syrup
A sprinkle of sesame to garnish
Beat the egg and add the flour and baking powder
Knead a soft dough and shape into small fingers
Place on a tray and bake 15 minutes at 190°C
Dip in the date syrup and sprinkle sesame
Semolina 60 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 60 g
Brown sugar 30 g
1 egg
Baking powder half a tsp
Blanched almonds for garnish, 6 pieces (optional)
Mix the semolina with the yogurt, brown sugar, egg and baking powder until well combined.
Let it rest 10 minutes so the semolina absorbs the moisture.
Pour into a small greased tin, arrange the almonds on top if desired and press gently.
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until set and golden, let cool slightly before slicing.
Egyptian or short-grain rice 40 g
Low-fat milk 400 ml
Cornflour 1 tsp
Brown sugar 25 g
Vanilla extract half a tsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon and a small cinnamon stick for garnish (optional)
Boil the rice in a little water for 10 minutes until it starts to soften, drain.
Add the milk and cook over medium-low heat 20-25 minutes, stirring frequently, until the rice is fully cooked.
Dissolve the cornflour in a little cold milk and add it with the brown sugar, cook 5 more minutes until the texture thickens.
Remove from the heat and add the vanilla, pour into serving cups, sprinkle with cinnamon and garnish with a cinnamon stick if desired, and serve warm or cold.
Thin kunafa shreds 60 g
Melted low-fat butter 2 tbsp
Low-fat cottage or ricotta cheese 80 g
Mixed nuts, coarsely chopped, 20 g
Honey or light sugar syrup 2 tbsp
A dash of orange blossom water (optional)
Rub the kunafa shreds with your hands to loosen them, mix with the melted butter until fully coated.
Place half the shreds in a small greased tin and press evenly.
Spread the cheese over it, cover with the other half of the shreds and press gently.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until golden and crisp, pour the honey or syrup over it while hot, sprinkle with nuts and orange blossom water if desired, and serve warm.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Warm water about 90 ml and a pinch of instant yeast
Brown sugar 1 tsp for the batter
Mixed nuts, coarsely chopped, 30 g for the filling
A pinch of ground cinnamon and brown sugar 1 tsp for the filling
Honey or light sugar syrup 1 tbsp to serve
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast and brown sugar gradually until a smooth liquid batter forms, let it rest 20-30 minutes until small bubbles appear.
Heat a non-stick pan, pour a tablespoon of batter to form a small disc, cook on one side only until bubbles appear and the surface dries, do not flip.
Repeat with the remaining batter, mix the nuts with the cinnamon and brown sugar for the filling.

Place a spoonful of filling on the uncooked side of each disc, fold in half and press the edges to seal like a clamshell, arrange on a lined tray and bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden, pour honey over them while hot and serve.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Warm water about 50 ml and a pinch of instant yeast
Brown sugar 1 tsp and a pinch of salt
1 tsp oil for the batter
Honey 2 tbsp to serve
A pinch of ground cinnamon (optional)
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast, brown sugar, salt and oil gradually until a thick, sticky batter forms, let it rest 30-40 minutes until roughly doubled in size.
Use two spoons to shape small balls of the batter and place on a lined tray with space between them.
Bake at 220°C for 14-16 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.
Pour honey over them while hot, sprinkle with cinnamon if desired, and serve immediately.
Low-fat milk 350 ml
Cornflour 2 tbsp
Brown sugar 25 g
Rosewater 1 tsp
Coarsely chopped pistachios 1 tbsp for garnish
A pinch of salt
Dissolve the cornflour in a quarter cup of the cold milk until smooth without lumps.
Heat the remaining milk with the brown sugar and salt in a pot over medium heat until nearly boiling.
Gradually stir in the cornflour mixture, stirring constantly, cook 5-7 minutes until the texture thickens like a creamy pudding.
Remove from the heat and add the rosewater, pour into serving cups, chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours, sprinkle with pistachios before serving.

name.en: Sahlab (Egyptian Warm Milk Dessert with Cinnamon and Nuts)

en: Low-fat milk 200 ml
Cornflour 1 tbsp
Brown sugar 1 tsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Coarsely chopped mixed nuts 1 tsp for garnish
A pinch of grated coconut for garnish (optional)
Dissolve the cornflour in a quarter cup of the cold milk until smooth without lumps.
Heat the remaining milk with the brown sugar in a small pot over medium heat until nearly boiling.
Gradually stir in the cornflour mixture, stirring constantly, cook 4-5 minutes until the texture thickens like a warm cream.
Pour into a serving cup, sprinkle with cinnamon, nuts and coconut if desired, and serve hot immediately.
Pitted dates, chopped, 80 g
Coarsely chopped walnuts 30 g
Whole-wheat flour 40 g
1 egg
A pinch of ground cinnamon and a pinch of baking powder
1 tsp oil for the tin
Mix the chopped dates with the cinnamon, baking powder and flour until combined.
Add the egg and mix well until a cohesive dough forms, add the walnuts and mix gently.
Pour into a small greased tin and press evenly.
Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until set and golden, let cool completely then cut into rectangular bars.
